listing.name: Blast Corps (Power Dozer)
listing.summary: A native Blast Corps player using your own USA revision 1 cartridge dump. Portcove manages the official Windows x64 and Linux x86-64 packages and preserves their default local game data; upstream owns original-game import.

steps.title: Choose your own original on first Play
steps.instruction: Choose your own Blast Corps USA revision 1 dump through the upstream in-process selector. It accepts .z64, .v64, .n64 or a single-ROM ZIP and checks normalized SHA-1 483f7161aea39de8b45c9fbc70a2c3883c4dea8c. The game stores its own normalized copy under data/cache/rom.z64. Core does not acquire or authenticate your cartridge dump; keep the original separately and do not share a data backup containing it.

steps.title: Use the complete Windows or Linux package
steps.instruction: The official Windows ZIP and Linux x86-64 archive follow the project’s stable release stream. Check the release notes for its testing status. Keep power-dozer.exe, its matching DLLs and notices together. Windows x64 needs SSSE3/SSE4.1, Vulkan drivers and the Microsoft Visual C++ x64 runtime linked in the packaged README. On Linux, keep power-dozer with its lib and licenses folders; it needs SSSE3/SSE4.1, glibc 2.38 or later, libz, Vulkan drivers, X11 or XWayland and a desktop file chooser. Portcove starts power-dozer directly, so the bundled Run Power Dozer.sh script is not needed. No game compiler or installer is required. Other platforms remain upstream-owned.

steps.title: Preserve game data and external diagnostics
steps.instruction: For the managed Windows and Linux routes, Portcove sets BLASTCORPS_DATA_DIR=data with the executable directory as working directory. It preserves the complete local data folder across compatible package updates and rollback, including cached original, EEPROM, committed Controller Pak data, settings, controls, backups and interrupted temporary files. A rollback does not rewind saves or guarantee that an older runtime reads newer state. In-progress Controller Pak game transactions follow upstream commit markers; this is not a guarantee of unsaved gameplay recovery. The separate RT64 diagnostics and ImGui profile remain external and outside Portcove backup/removal: %LOCALAPPDATA%/blastcorps-feasibility on Windows, and ~/.config/.blastcorps-feasibility on Linux, or ~/.blastcorps-feasibility when ~/.config does not exist. Keep a separate backup of actual custom --data-dir, capture or debug paths; Portcove does not import or migrate them. Close the actual player before deliberate external changes.

steps.title: Keep one replacement owner
steps.instruction: Use Portcove for the managed copy and upstream/player ownership for separately registered installations. Existing external copies and custom profile paths retain their own update and preservation responsibility. Package integrity and first-party fixtures do not establish gameplay, real-save restoration or every graphics device.
